messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: High rate of OOM/retry on inference hosts in eu-west-1. Alert: kv_cache_fragmentation > 80% for multiple GPU workers, continuous-batching queue length spiked. Investigate ASAP.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a big jump in kv arena free/used ratio on node gpu-eu-12. errors look like CUDA OOM / torch::cuda::OutOfMemoryError in the logs.

maya (oncall): quick summary so far: 10:02 UTC spike, sustained for ~8m, ~30% of requests seeing >500ms token latency + some retries. No full node reboots yet.

prod-support: FYI a handful of paid customers reported degraded responses around 10:05 UTC — mostly small batch jobs. No SLA breach yet but customers asking.

linh (eng-runtime): picking up logs from gpu-eu-12:
```
[10:02:11] kv_cache: arena total=12288MB used=10120MB free_frag=2160MB
[10:02:11] torch.cuda.caching_allocator: couldn't allocate 256MB, trying to free cached blocks
[10:02:12] continuous_batcher: flush triggered (max_latency 120ms exceeded)
```
looks like fragmentation is causing inability to satisfy mid-sized allocations.

ash (eng-ml): this smells like the recent batching change that increased prefix concat and some quantized kernels; more frequent small allocations from the kv cache could be fragmenting the allocation arena. did we just push a batch config change?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.15-build-4556 -> prod completed at 09:58 UTC (canary passed).

maya (oncall): yes, build-4556 included continuous-batching tweak: batch.target_tokens increased from 1024 -> 2048 and batch.window_ms relaxed. reverting that would be disruptive but might confirm cause.

tj (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) toggle the batching tweak back via runtime flag (fast, per-cluster) 2) adjust PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to set max_split_size_mb to reduce fragmentation 3) run a targeted arena compaction job (risk: pauses). Which do we want first?

ops: I'm ready to flip the runtime flag. Can we do a scoped rollback on eu-west-1 only?

maya (oncall): yes, prefer region-scoped change. Do we have a runtime knob? I think `runtime.flags.continuous_batching.enabled=false` exists per-cluster.

linh (eng-runtime): confirmed: we expose per-cluster overrides. Command: 
```bash
adminctl config set cluster/eu-west-1/runtime.flags.continuous_batching.target_tokens=1024 --apply
```
I can run this and push a canary to 5% of nodes first.

ash (eng-ml): while we do that, also set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 in the allocator env for the same canary hosts. That tends to limit large-block splitting and helps with fragmentation without full restart.

ops: doing canary now. running command: `adminctl config set ... target_tokens=1024 --canary=5%`

deploy-bot: config change queued: change id cfg-20260315-31, canary 5% started.

maya (oncall): observing metrics... kv_cache_fragmentation metric already down from 82% -> 68% on canary hosts. latency tail improved a bit.

prod-support: Customers on the canary nodes are reporting much better responses (two customers pinged).

linh (eng-runtime): initiating env patch on the same canary set:
```bash
adminctl shell run-on-hosts --canary=5% --cmd "export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128"
```
Note: this uses our hot-env mechanism; no container restart but alloc conf may not take effect until next model load.

tj (sre): we should also schedule a compaction run during a low-traffic window to reclaim fragmented blocks. I'll prepare a job that iterates GPUs and triggers `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` + controlled allocator compaction; will require brief reduced throughput on each host.

ops: canary to 25% in flight per runbook if metrics keep improving. Ready to scale.

maya (oncall): metrics: after 12m of canary adjustments fragmentation down to 55% cluster-wide (canary hosts in eu-west-1), request retry rate down 4x. I'm recommending ramp to 50% now.

ash (eng-ml): note: if fragmentation persists after env changes, we should consider changing arena sizing: set kv.arena_target_mb to a larger multiple to reduce churn. But that is heavier.

ops: ramping canary to 50% -> command executed.

deploy-bot: cfg-20260315-31 canary=50% passed basic health checks at 10:28 UTC.

maya (oncall): customer impact update: 6 affected customers initially, 4 have confirmed improvement, 2 still on non-canary nodes (will be covered by next ramp). No escalations.

linh (eng-runtime): compiled recent allocator traces: a pattern of many 32-128KB allocations and frees causing free-list fragmentation. Long-lived KV entries + mid-sized transient allocations are a bad combo. I'll add better sampling to the allocator logs for postmortem.

tj (sre): plan for the next hour: 1) finish ramp to 100% in eu-west-1 if trends hold 2) schedule controlled compaction for off-peak window (11:30 UTC) 3) run job to adjust arena_target_mb if compaction insufficient.

ops: executing final ramp to 100% now.

deploy-bot: cfg-20260315-31 rolled to 100% eu-west-1 at 10:33 UTC.

maya (oncall): final metrics at 10:40 UTC: fragmentation down to 38% cluster-wide eu-west-1, token latency tails back to baseline, retry rate near zero. Marking incident as mitigated.

prod-support: customers on eu-west-1 all reporting normal behavior. No SLA incidents.

nick (devex): can we add a short blurb to status page summarizing cause and mitigation? customers appreciate transparency.

maya (oncall): yes. I'll draft. quick note: root cause appears to be interaction between increased batch target size (build-4556) and existing allocator behavior causing KV arena fragmentation under heavier mid-sized allocation churn. Hotfix: rollback batch target and set allocator soft limit (PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF) as short-term fix. Follow-ups: allocator logging, compaction job, and long-term arena tuning.

maya (oncall): Post-incident actions (assigned):
- linh: add allocator sampling & traces (ETA 48h)
- ash: run workload sims to validate batch.target_tokens = 2048 with arena_target_mb increases (ETA 72h)
- tj: schedule compaction runbook and automate low-cpu pauses (ETA 24h)
- ops: add a preflight perf check for batch tuning changes (ETA 72h)

maya (oncall): closing the pager. If any regression reappears ping #incidents immediately. :white_check_mark:
